questions.q: In the three-sector circular flow model, which of the following represents a leakage from the circular flow? (a) Government purchases (G) (b) Transfer payments (c) Taxes (T) (d) Subsidies
questions.a: Correct answer: (c) Taxes (T). Taxes are a withdrawal of income from households and firms, reducing the flow of spending. Government purchases (G) and transfer payments are injections; subsidies are also injections (negative taxes). A student who picks (a) or (b) confuses government spending with leakage. A student who picks (d) misunderstands that subsidies add to firms' revenue.

questions.q: Explain why imports (M) are treated as a leakage in the four-sector circular flow model, while exports (X) are an injection. Use the flow of money and goods in your answer.
questions.a: Imports represent domestic income spent on foreign-produced goods — money flows out of the domestic circular flow to the rest of the world, reducing domestic demand. Exports represent foreign spending on domestic goods — money flows into the domestic circular flow from the rest of the world, increasing domestic demand. A wrong answer that says "imports bring goods in, so they are an injection" confuses real flow (goods) with monetary flow (payment). The circular flow model tracks money payments; goods flow opposite to money.

questions.q: An economy has the following data (in ₹ crore): C = 5,000, I = 1,200, G = 1,500, X = 800, M = 600. Calculate (i) GDP using the expenditure method, (ii) total leakages, (iii) total injections, and (iv) verify the equilibrium condition.
questions.a: (i) GDP = C + I + G + (X - M) = 5,000 + 1,200 + 1,500 + (800 - 600) = ₹7,900 crore. (ii) Leakages = S + T + M. We don't have S and T directly, but in equilibrium leakages = injections. (iii) Injections = I + G + X = 1,200 + 1,500 + 800 = ₹3,500 crore. (iv) Equilibrium requires S + T + M = I + G + X. Since M = 600, we need S + T = 2,900. A student who forgets to subtract M in GDP or adds M to injections makes a sign error. A student who uses C + I + G + X + M double-counts imports.

questions.q: Compare the equilibrium condition in the two-sector model (S = I) with the four-sector model (S + T + M = I + G + X). If the government runs a budget deficit (G > T) and the economy has a trade deficit (M > X), what must be true about private saving (S) relative to private investment (I) for equilibrium to hold?
questions.a: From S + T + M = I + G + X, rearrange: S - I = (G - T) + (X - M). If G > T (budget deficit) and M > X (trade deficit, so X - M < 0), then (G - T) + (X - M) could be positive, negative, or zero depending on magnitudes. For equilibrium, S - I must equal that sum. A common error is to assume S > I always; actually S could be less than I if the trade deficit outweighs the budget deficit. The student must algebraically manipulate the identity, not guess.

questions.q: "In a four-sector economy, a rise in the marginal propensity to import (MPM) reduces the size of the multiplier." Evaluate this statement. Does it hold in the simple circular flow model without multiplier analysis? Explain.
questions.a: The statement is about the multiplier (a Keynesian cross concept), not the circular flow identity itself. The circular flow model only shows the accounting identity S + T + M = I + G + X at equilibrium; it does not contain behavioural parameters like MPM or the multiplier. In the circular flow framework, a higher MPM means more leakage per unit of income, so for a given level of injections, equilibrium income will be lower — but the model doesn't quantify "by how much" without a consumption function and multiplier derivation. A student who says "yes, because MPM is a leakage" confuses the static identity with the dynamic multiplier process.

questions.q: Construct a four-sector circular flow diagram for an economy where households save ₹200 crore, pay ₹300 crore in taxes, and spend ₹150 crore on imports. Firms invest ₹250 crore. The government spends ₹400 crore. Exports are ₹100 crore. Label all flows, show the equilibrium condition numerically, and state whether the economy is in equilibrium. If not, which direction will income adjust?
questions.a: Leakages = S + T + M = 200 + 300 + 150 = ₹650 crore. Injections = I + G + X = 250 + 400 + 100 = ₹750 crore. Since leakages (650) < injections (750), the economy is not in equilibrium; there is excess demand. Income will rise (firms experience unplanned inventory depletion, increase output). A good diagram shows households → firms (C), firms → households (factor payments), government ↔ households/firms (T, G, transfers), foreign sector ↔ domestic (X, M). A poor answer draws only three sectors or mislabels M as injection.
